patch_description: The current best program spends most of its 9.86s in `_local_shift_search`, where every candidate shift re-solves all 26 radii from scratch (300 Gauss-Seidel iterations × 4 directions × 26 circles × multiple sweeps). This rewrite keeps the proven seed + refine + pressure-perturb pipeline but replaces the evaluation core with an incremental, warm-started solver: (1) the distance matrix is cached and only the row/column of the moved circle is updated when testing a shift, (2) the radius vector is warm-started from the previous solution so radii re-converge in a handful of Gauss-Seidel passes instead of 300, and (3) the saved time is reinvested into a finer delta scale (0.0005) and a second full shift-search round after `_greedy_enlarge` to harvest the slack that greedy enlargement exposes — exactly the strategy recommended in the feedback. Vectorized NumPy distance updates replace the Python loops for further speed.
